author: Taylor Beam STAFF WRITER
title: Local chapters gear up to celebrate National FFA Week | WV News | wvnews.com
text:
CLARKSBURG, W.Va — Local FFA chapters are gearing up to celebrate National FFA Week, Feb. 21-28. Bridgeport High School’s club is anticipating a packed schedule.
“Next week is a celebration of our youth nationwide,” Justin Arnold, Bridgeport High School FFA adviser and agriculture teacher, said. “Just being able to reflect on the triumphs and the traditions that have been set forth throughout the history of this nation’s agriculture.”
“FFA as an organization, from the theming to the traditions, is the embodiment of American culture while highlighting the backbone of America, that being agriculture,” Arnold said.
Arnold’s chapter has about 40 active members and he has advised the group for about 3 1/2 years. To celebrate, the group will host and participate in events every day of the week.
“Chapters at the local level will do different things to celebrate,” Arnold said. “We have spirit days for the school, activities during the day for all students and chapter-exclusive activities after school.”
To kick off the week, Bridgeport will join Lincoln High’s FFA in traveling to the Jackson’s Mill Rodeo, hosted by McCray Cattle Company. The event will include FFA-themed activities to celebrate the occasion.
Bridgeport High homerooms will compete in an agricultural quiz bowl throughout the week. The winning classroom will be crowned champion and receive a pizza party, courtesy of the FFA.
“On Friday morning, we have our fourth annual first responders breakfast,” Arnold said. “Students are the chefs that day from 8 to 10 a.m. and are opening the doors to all Harrison County first responders.”
FFA has changed and evolved over the years. Some may think of it as an organization focused on raising farm animals and crops, but FFA is about much more.
“Most people recall it back in the day as Future Farmers of America, but they changed their name to encompass a more diverse group of membership,” Arnold said. “For students within FFA, the one thing that unites them is a passion and an interest in agriculture.”
“Fifty or 60 years ago, our definition of agriculture was kind of traditional farming, but there are so many careers that fall within the agricultural realm,” Arnold said. “I have students who are wanting to be veterinarians, marine biologists, ag teachers and plant pathologists.”
“I like to tell students, we have different political problems, economic problems and all these things that get global attention, but not a single one of these issues is solved on an empty stomach,” Arnold said. “All of those people are fed ... because of agriculture.”
Since agriculture is a central piece of society, Arnold makes sure to remind students of job security within the industry. He also sees FFA as an opportunity to expose youth to a variety of skill sets.
“The amount of students that I’ve seen just in three years come in with really bad social anxiety, some things that have really been setting them back in life,” Arnold said. “It’s crazy looking at some of these students who are now juniors and seniors ... and think about how many times they’ve stood in front of a crowd and spoken.”
“Generally speaking, FFA has a lot of soft skills that are underlying all of the different events and contests that students are a part of,” Arnold said. “A lot of the students become better at studying, they become more organized, motivated and dedicated to a cause.”
Arnold was a member of FFA in school and it changed his life, setting him on the path he is on today. He sees the program as a unique opportunity for students to develop.
His students have traveled all over the state and country through FFA. They show cattle, learn about floriculture and meet others with a similar passion for agriculture. Next week, Bridgeport FFA will join chapters around the country in celebrating their achievements and agriculture as a whole.
